claims.label: PROVED
claims.statement: SAT is not decidable by any deterministic polynomial-time multitape Turing machine; this is equivalent to P != NP.
claims.computational_model: Deterministic multitape Turing machine on a fixed binary SAT encoding
claims.fan_in: Encoded formulas use fan-in two AND/OR and fan-in one NOT
claims.asymptotic_quantifiers: For every machine M and constant c, some input violates correctness or the n^c+c bound
claims.case_regime: Worst-case exact decision; total language; no promise

claims.label: PROVED
claims.statement: If SAT has no polynomial-size general Boolean circuit family, then P != NP.
claims.computational_model: General acyclic Boolean circuits and deterministic multitape Turing machines
claims.circuit_size: All O(n^k) sizes for every fixed k
claims.advice: Polynomial advice is represented by the circuit family
claims.asymptotic_quantifiers: If one SAT language defeats every fixed polynomial circuit exponent, then it defeats uniform polynomial time
claims.case_regime: Worst-case exact decision; total language; no promise

claims.label: PROVED
claims.statement: If one language in NP is outside P/poly, then P != NP; Cook-Levin reductions also give SAT outside P/poly.
claims.computational_model: NP verifier, polynomial-time many-one reductions, and general Boolean circuits
claims.asymptotic_quantifiers: Exists one L in NP such that for every exponent d no O(n^d) circuit family decides L
claims.case_regime: Worst-case exact decision; total language; no promise

claims.label: PROVED
claims.statement: There are recursive oracles A and B with P^A=NP^A and P^B!=NP^B.
claims.computational_model: Deterministic and nondeterministic polynomial-time oracle Turing machines
claims.uniformity: Uniform machines relative to a fixed oracle
claims.oracle_access: Arbitrary recursive oracle, one fixed oracle per relativized world
claims.asymptotic_quantifiers: Exists recursive A giving equality and exists recursive B giving separation

claims.label: CONDITIONAL
claims.statement: Under strong pseudorandom-function assumptions, constructive large properties cannot be useful against polynomial-size general circuits in the Razborov-Rudich sense.
claims.computational_model: Algorithms deciding properties of Boolean truth tables and general Boolean circuits
claims.uniformity: Uniform property algorithm; non-uniform circuit target
claims.circuit_size: Polynomial-size target circuits; parameters as in RR97
claims.randomness: Cryptographic pseudorandomness occurs in the hypothesis; property constructivity is algorithmic
claims.advice: As specified by the natural-proofs framework
claims.asymptotic_quantifiers: Conditional on existence of sufficiently hard pseudorandom functions; property is large and constructive across lengths
claims.case_regime: Boolean function property; worst-case usefulness and density condition

claims.label: PROVED
claims.statement: Relativization augmented with low-degree extensions forms an algebrization barrier for covered proof techniques.
claims.computational_model: Oracle complexity classes with algebraic low-degree extensions
claims.uniformity: Relativized uniform machines; non-uniform circuits where stated by the source
claims.circuit_size: Source-dependent; no terminal general-circuit size conclusion consumed
claims.advice: Source-dependent; explicit where circuits are non-uniform
claims.oracle_access: Arbitrary oracle and its low-degree extension
claims.field_or_algebraic_model: Finite-field low-degree extensions as defined in AW09
claims.asymptotic_quantifiers: Oracle constructions quantify over relativized/algebraically extended worlds as stated in AW09
claims.case_regime: Barrier theorem, not a terminal language lower bound

claims.label: PROVED
claims.statement: A superpolynomial-factor improvement for general Circuit-SAT for every polynomial circuit-size exponent implies NEXP is not contained in P/poly.
claims.computational_model: Deterministic or co-nondeterministic Circuit-SAT algorithm and general Boolean circuits
claims.circuit_size: Input circuits n^k for every fixed k; polynomial-size target
claims.advice: None in canonical premise; polynomial non-uniformity in target
claims.asymptotic_quantifiers: One superpolynomial saving s(n); algorithm for every fixed k

claims.label: PROVED
claims.statement: NEXP is not contained in non-uniform ACC0; the proof uses a class-specific SAT algorithm and transfer theorem.
claims.computational_model: ACC0 circuits and nondeterministic exponential-time Turing machines
claims.uniformity: Uniform hard-language class; non-uniform circuit target
claims.circuit_size: Polynomial, with quasipolynomial strengthening in the source
claims.fan_in: Unbounded AND/OR/MOD_m; NOT as permitted by ACC0
claims.field_or_algebraic_model: Modular gates, not an algebraic computation model
claims.asymptotic_quantifiers: One NEXP language defeats all polynomial-size ACC0 families

claims.label: PROVED
claims.statement: A nondeterministic GAP-C-UNSAT algorithm in O(2^((1-epsilon)n)) time on size 2^(epsilon n) circuits implies for all k that NTIME[n^(c k^4/epsilon)] is not contained in C-SIZE[n^k].
claims.computational_model: Nondeterministic gap-unsatisfiability algorithm, nondeterministic time classes, and typical C circuits
claims.uniformity: Uniform algorithm and language class; non-uniform circuit target
claims.circuit_depth: Class C dependent and must be instantiated
claims.fan_in: Class C dependent and must be instantiated
claims.field_or_algebraic_model: None unless instantiated C includes algebraic gates
claims.asymptotic_quantifiers: Fixed epsilon; exists c; for every fixed k a class noncontainment whose witness language may depend on k
claims.case_regime: Promise/gap: UNSAT versus at least 1/4 satisfying; worst-case on promised inputs

claims.label: PROVED
claims.statement: If NP is contained in P/poly, then the polynomial hierarchy collapses to its second level.
claims.computational_model: Polynomial-hierarchy oracle Turing machines and general Boolean circuit/advice computation
claims.advice: Polynomial advice allowed in P/poly premise
claims.oracle_access: Hierarchy quantifiers/oracles in class characterization; no external oracle
claims.asymptotic_quantifiers: If every NP language has some polynomial circuit family, PH equals its second level

claims.label: PROVED
claims.statement: For every fixed k, some language L_k in P lacks P-uniform O(n^k)-size circuits.
claims.computational_model: Deterministic polynomial-time Turing machines and P-uniform Boolean circuits
claims.circuit_size: O(n^k) for one fixed k per language
claims.advice: No arbitrary advice; circuits have the stated uniform generator
claims.asymptotic_quantifiers: For every k exists a possibly different L_k in P

claims.label: NO-GO
claims.statement: The audited Williams transfers cannot be promoted directly, without a new separation mechanism, from high-class or fixed-exponent conclusions to SAT outside P/poly.
claims.computational_model: Circuit-SAT meta-algorithms, nondeterministic time classes, and general Boolean circuits
claims.uniformity: Uniform algorithm premise; non-uniform desired conclusion
claims.circuit_size: Polynomial input circuits and all polynomial target sizes
claims.advice: None in premise; polynomial non-uniformity in desired conclusion
claims.asymptotic_quantifiers: Failure is the unsupported swap from forall k exists L_k to exists L forall k
claims.case_regime: Worst-case exact decision, plus explicit gap promise where BR-MW18 is used

claims.label: PROVED
claims.statement: A uniformly verifiable hard-language family with efficiently computable padding exponents and unbounded circuit-exponent to verifier-exponent ratio pads into one NP language outside P/poly.
claims.computational_model: Uniformly indexed nondeterministic verifier and general Boolean circuits
claims.circuit_size: Source excludes O(n^b(j)); target excludes every O(N^d)
claims.advice: None for verifier; polynomial advice represented by circuits
claims.asymptotic_quantifiers: One effective family with unary-polynomial-time computable exponents; limsup b(j)/a(j)=infinity; one target language against every d

claims.label: EXPLORATORY
claims.statement: Construct unconditionally a uniformly verifiable family with efficiently computable padding exponents, unrestricted circuit lower bounds, and limsup b(j)/a(j)=infinity.
claims.computational_model: Uniformly indexed nondeterministic multitape verifier and general Boolean circuits
claims.circuit_size: O(n^b(j)) lower bounds with unbounded b(j)/a(j)
claims.advice: None for verifier; arbitrary polynomial non-uniformity in target
claims.asymptotic_quantifiers: One effective family; every j has an infinitely-often lower bound; exponent ratio has infinite limsup
